CME first seen to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2026-06-04T04:24Z. This front fades quickly. It is no longer visible by the time it reaches the edge of the FOV of SOHO LASCO C2, so it is only seen in SOHO LASCO C2 and very faintly for a couple frames in STEREO A COR2. The source of this CME is most likely field line movement seen beyond the NW limb in GOES SUVI 284 starting around 2026-06-04T03:30Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement chosen because this CME is only visible in a single coronagraph and because the source is far-sided.

data.note: Faint, narrow CME first seen to the SSW in STEREO A COR2 beginning around 2026-06-04T06:23Z. It is also seen to the SSW in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1. The CME is mostly missed by SOHO LASCO C2 because the CME start time is covered by a short data gap. The source of this CME is likely an eruption with southward-directed ejecta seen near the W limb in GOES SUVI 304 beginning around 2026-06-04T04:40Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit among SOHO LASCO C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2.

data.note: Faint CME first seen to the SW in GOES CCOR-1 starting around 2026-06-04T10:00Z. This front is also seen to the SW in STEREO A COR2 but was missed by SOHO LASCO C2/C3 in real time due to a downlink gap. The source is most likely some ejecta seen leaving the western limb in GOES SUVI 304 beginning around 2026-06-04T08:52Z. This is one in an hours long series of similar eruptions.

cmeAnalyses.note: Approximate measurement based on best fit between STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1. There is a higher degree of uncertainty in this measurement due to the faintness of the front.

data.note: Fast, narrow CME first seen to the SW in STEREO A COR2 and to the S in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. A potential source is visible as moving/opening field lines along the southern limb in GOES SUVI 284 after the start time of the CME from STEREO A's perspective. Additionally, there is an eruption visible along/just beyond the SW limb in STEREO A EUVI 195 starting around 2026-06-04T16:35Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on best fit using SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

data.note: Faint CME observed to the W in SOHO LASCO C2, fading into background after several frames. The source is likely AR 14458, with field line movement and dimming starting around 2026-06-04T20:22Z in SDO AIA 193 centered around S07W23. Additional dimming centered ~S25E30 triggered shortly after the first eruption.

cmeAnalyses.note: SOHO LASCO C2 only 3D analysis using the observed source longitude centered around W23, as such the parameters could vary slightly. CME fades after several frames in C2's field-of-view.

data.note: Faint CME observed to the W in SOHO LASCO C2/3 and GOES CCOR-1, fading into background late in LASCO C2 and early in LASCO C3/GOES CCOR-1. The source is likely AR 14458, with field line movement and dimming starting around 2026-06-04T22:40Z in SDO AIA 193 centered around S03W17.

cmeAnalyses.note: SOHO LASCO C2 only 3D analysis using the observed source longitude centered around W17, as such the parameters could vary slightly. CME fades quickly in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1. CME half width may be slightly below 10 degrees.

data.note: CME observed to the NW only in STEREO A COR2, perhaps due to the occulting disks of LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 obscuring visibility. No distinct source for this front is observed outside of some weak filament movement, without clearly erupting, near STEREO A's southwest limb in STEREO A EUVI 195 spanning approximately 2026-06-05T02:55Z - 2026-06-05T07:25Z. This front is quickly overlapped by significant CME: 2026-06-05T09:09Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: STEREO A only plane of sky, taken at W149.9 with STEREO A's current location at W59.9.

data.note: Far-sided halo CME to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, and wide front observed to the W in STEREO A COR2. The source is far-sided from Earth and likely STEREO A (W59.9) as well, should be well observed by Solar Orbiter (E156.3) when its data is available. The source is more directly observed in STEREO A EUVI 195/304 on or beyond STEREO's limb (~W149.9) as a filament eruption and field line movement starting around 2026-06-05T08:15Z. It is also observed in GOES SUVI 195/284, and less prominent in SDO AIA 171/193/211 with its closer field-of-view, as wide opening field lines and EUV wave over the SE limb starting around 2026-06-05T09:00Z. Latest Solar Orbiter EUI 304 imagery at 2026-06-0500:01Z shows numerous filaments resting around the W180-E150 and N15-S30 range surrounding former Active Regions 14439 and 14442, for potential candidates. Likely associated with an estimated M3 [M2,M6] flare observed by Solar Orbiter STIX peaking at 2026-06-05T08:58Z.

The shock front is complex and has two distinct edges, this analysis is of the "brighter" SE-directed inner shock (ahead of and distinct from the bright LE), excluding a faint more SW-directed shock edge as fitting both in one does not yield a good fit.

The shock front is complex and has two distinct edges, this analysis is of the "more faint" SW-directed outer shock, excluding a bright more SE-directed shock edge as fitting both in one does not yield a good fit.

data.note: Faint CME front observed to the NW only in STEREO A COR2. No clear source for this CME is observed in SDO AIA, GOES SUVI, or STEREO A EUVI, although it could be outflow following significant CME: 2026-06-05T09:09Z from a far-sided filament eruption that triangulated around E160 earlier in the day.

cmeAnalyses.note: STEREO A plane-of-sky taken at W149.9, with STEREO A currently located at W59.9.

data.note: Faint CME front observed to the NE only in STEREO A COR2. No clear source for this CME is observed in SDO AIA, GOES SUVI, or STEREO A EUVI.

cmeAnalyses.note: STEREO A plane-of-sky taken at E30.1, with STEREO A currently located at W59.9.

data.note: Faint CME to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2 and GOES CCOR-1, and NE in STEREO A COR2, pylon obscured in LASCO C3. The source is a C4.1 flare from AR 14455 which peaked at 2026-06-05T15:03Z observed in SDO AIA 131, also observed as field line movement and small dimming in SDO AIA 171/193.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. The CME appears deflected northward and tracks askew with the swpc_cat tool, as such the parameters could vary slightly, with high confidence in the out-of-ecliptic direction.

data.note: Narrow CME first seen to the ne by STEREO A COR2 beginning at 2026-06-05T16:09Z. This CME is either directed into the pylon or occulting disk in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, and is therefore not clearly visible. There is no clear source that fits the CME seen for this event.

cmeAnalyses.note: STEREO A plane-of-sky measurement using a longitude of E30.1 (as STEREO A is currently located at W59.9) due to lack of clear source an coronagraph imagery to triangulate.

data.note: CME first seen to the SW by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-06-05T23:24Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. This CME is not seen in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap which began at 2026-06-05T19:09Z. The source of this event is field line opening seen along the SW limb in SDO AIA 171 beginning at 2026-06-05T22:00Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement using a longitude of W90 due to source location near the limb and lack of SOHO/GOES coronagraph imagery to triangulate.

data.note: This CME is visible to the southeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The source is likely far-sided as there are no source signatures on the Earth-facing disk around the time of this event.

cmeAnalyses.note: A plane-of-sky measurement was made using a longitude of -90 degrees due to the far-sided and therefore unknown source location.

data.note: This CME is visible to the north in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and to the northeast in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is unknown, but may be related to faint field line movement visible over the northeast limb in SDO AIA 171 starting around 2026-06-06T03:00Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

data.note: This CME is visible to the southwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is a far-sided eruption visible on the southwest limb in STEREO A EUVI 304 imagery starting around 2026-06-06T13:15Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

data.note: This CME is visible as a southeast partial halo in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery, and is seen to the east in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is an eruption and M1.8 flare from Active Region 14461 (S22E24) starting around 2025-06-06T13:45Z as seen in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304, GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304, and STEREO A EUVI 195/304 imagery. An opening of field lines is visible over the southeast limb in STEREO A EUVI 195 imagery, and a large EUV wave and dimming is observed surrounding the eruption site in SDO AIA 193 and GOES SUVI 195/284 imagery. Additionally, post eruptive arcades are visible in SDO AIA 171/193 and GOES SUVI 171/105 imagery starting around 2026-06-06T15:00Z.

data.note: Faint CME observed to the E in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, not seen in STEREO A COR2. The source may be field line movement in SDO AIA starting around 2026-06-06T16:34Z over the E limb around S10, or AR 14464 with slow brightening near S09E63, the movement is not too clear where it traces on-disk.

data.note: CME observed to the S in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, not in STEREO A COR2 during a data gap spanning 2026-06-06T19:09Z to 2026-06-06T23:09Z. The source is a filament eruption far-sided from Earth, observed in STEREO A EUVI 304 at 2026-06-06T19:15Z as filament ejecta on/near its west limb, putting it at approximately W150 with STEREO A currently located at W60. Also observed as filament ejecta over the S limb in GOES SUVI 304.

data.note: Bright, relatively narrow CME seen to the southeast in SOHO LASCO C2, C3, and STEREO A COR2A, along with GOES CCOR-1 likely associated with a far-sided eruption.
